en.title: Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth Director Fought For Disc Version Amid Digital Shift
en.summary: The director of Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, Naoki Hamaguchi, has revealed his personal efforts to include a disc version for the upcoming game. This comes as the gaming industry continues its rapid transition towards an all-digital future.
en.body:
The path to **Final Fantasy VII Rebirth** has been paved with passionate fan discussions, and one of the most persistent has revolved around physical media. Director **Naoki Hamaguchi** has now offered a candid look into his own advocacy for a disc version of the highly anticipated title, even as the industry increasingly embraces digital-only releases.

"I did my best to fight for a disc release," **Hamaguchi** stated in a recent interview with Radio Times, acknowledging the industry's trajectory towards a "future where physical media is essentially disc-less." For **Hamaguchi**, the appreciation for tangible game copies runs deep, stemming from childhood memories of collecting physical editions. "Personally, obviously, I bought lots of physical editions of games as a child," he shared. "Sometimes I buy digital editions of games, but if I'm particularly attached to a title, I want to get the physical version." He also noted the personal significance of having physical copies to get signed by friends or acquaintances who worked on the game, highlighting the sentimental value that digital formats cannot replicate.

While **Final Fantasy VII Rebirth** will indeed offer a disc option for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X players when it launches in 2027, it's not without its caveats. Owners who opt for the physical version will find that the full game experience necessitates a substantial additional download, a detail that has understandably divided some segments of the fanbase. **Hamaguchi** and the team at Square Enix, however, maintain that this decision was not taken lightly. "I do really like and appreciate physical media," **Hamaguchi** reiterated, understanding the sentiment of fans who declare, "No disc, no purchase."

## The Physical vs. Digital Divide

The conversation around physical media in gaming is a sensitive one, particularly for long-time enthusiasts who cherish the act of owning and displaying their game collections. The confirmation that **Final Fantasy VII Rebirth** will include a disc, albeit one that acts more as a "key disc" containing only the opening sequences, is a compromise that attempts to bridge the gap. For many, the idea of a game requiring a massive download even with a physical disc feels like a step away from the traditional ownership model. This sentiment echoes across online forums and social media, where players express both gratitude for the disc option and frustration over its limitations.

## What's Next

**Final Fantasy VII Rebirth** is slated for release in 2027. Further details regarding the exact size of the required download for physical editions and any potential regional differences are expected to be announced closer to the launch date.

"And you know, being in the industry, sometimes I want to get my friends or acquaintances who've worked on something to sign a copy of their own game." Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is confirmed to have a disc option when it launches in 2027, but there are some caveats. When physical owners on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, for example, pop their discs in, they should know the full experience will require an additional download – and a hefty one at that . It's a decision that has some fans split, but not one Hamaguchi and the team at Square Enix took lightly . "I do really like and appreciate physical media," he said. "I see a lot of people on social media saying, 'No disc, no purchase,' and I understand where they're coming from." Hamaguchi acknowledged that Final Fantasy 7 Revelation does have a disc alternative for those who want it, even if it's just a "key disc" that only has "the opening." He added that he understands that "there are people out there with a lot of opinions" about the future of physical media and shared a message to those who feel most passionately about the issue. "First of all, I've got people saying to me on social media, 'Give us a full disc version!' And so, from an overall perspective, let me first say that as the director, it's my responsibility to look after the content of the game to make sure it's fun, really exciting," he said. Then, smiling, he added, "The product line-up, the SKUs (stock keeping units), how it's going on sale; that is the responsibility of the publishing team. So, my authority there is somewhat limited." Despite the "pressure" for disc-less editions and digital editions, Hamaguchi said he "used my position to put forth an argument for the physical version as much as possible." That resulted in negotiations, "both internally and with first parties," leading to Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's one-disc strategy. He added, "I completely understand there are those out there who may not really agree with that direction or approve of that direction," but it's what he fought for, and it's the best result he could conjure.
